explanation: For y1=e^{-4x} and y2=e^{3x}, the Wronskian is 7e^{-x}. Variation of parameters gives u1=-∫2x dx=-x² and u2=∫2xe^{-7x} dx=-(2/49)(7x+1)e^{-7x}. Hence yp=-(x²+2x/7+2/49)e^{-4x}. Absorbing the homogeneous term -(2/49)e^{-4x} into A gives option a. Directly, if g=e^{-4x}v with v=-x²-2x/7, then g''+g'-12g=e^{-4x}(v''-7v')=14xe^{-4x}.
